open_points.subject: listener opening order
open_points.text: “opens the listener of each surface” and “One that cannot be opened stops the start with a diagnostic naming the surface”
open_points.question: In which order are the service API and owner-interface listeners opened, so which surface supplies the first-failure diagnostic when neither address can be opened?
options: Open the service API listener first
open_points.default_guess: Open the service API listener first, following the order in which the two surfaces are otherwise named.

witness.initial: Both release-fixed listener addresses are unavailable.
events: module:instance_lifecycle attempts to open the listeners and must stop at the first failure.
outcomes: The diagnostic names the service API, because its listener was attempted first.
The diagnostic names the owner interface, because its listener was attempted first.
witness.observer: The owner reading the start diagnostic

open_points.subject: refused owner request and idle timeout
open_points.text: Step 2 says “The arrival restarts the 30 minutes”; Errors says a request with a valid session but a missing or wrong CSRF value is refused and “nothing changes.”
open_points.question: Does a refused change carrying a valid owner session but an invalid CSRF value restart that session’s 30-minute idle period?
options: Restart the idle period because the valid session request arrived
Leave the idle period unchanged because the request was refused
open_points.default_guess: Restart the idle period, following A13 and step 2.

witness.initial: A valid owner session will reach 30 minutes of inactivity in one minute.
events: The owner interface receives a change request carrying the valid session cookie but no valid CSRF value.
Two minutes later the owner sends a valid request.
outcomes: The refused request restarted the idle period, so the later request is admitted.
Nothing changed on refusal, so the session has expired and the later request is refused.
witness.observer: The owner making the later request

open_points.subject: refused confirmation when both confirmation and import closure fail
open_points.text: “A confirmation refused because another session's import closed it: ... no step is shown again” versus “Any other refused confirmation: ... the step is to be shown again.”
open_points.question: Which outcome applies when another session has closed the import, but the submitting session first fails the stage-(1) confirmation check, so the closure is not reached under the first-failure rule?
options: Classify by the first failure and show the step again
Classify by the existing closure and refuse the import permanently without another step
open_points.default_guess: Treat the closure as final and never show another import confirmation step.

witness.initial: Session A has an import confirmation value that has expired; session B has a valid import confirmation.
events: Session B confirms successfully, writes the closure, and drops every session’s upload.
Session A submits its expired confirmation value.
module:owner_sessions refuses it at stage (1) and clears it, before migration_import is reached.
outcomes: It is an “other refused confirmation,” so the text says the step is shown again.
Because the closure exists, A16 rule 8 and the closure-specific outcome prohibit showing the step again.

open_points.subject: failure to remove the unencrypted snapshot
open_points.text: “removes the unencrypted copy before going on — a copy it cannot remove fails the run and is left ...; the backup records ... decrypts it ... [and] a backup that passes is renamed to its kept name”
open_points.question: After encryption succeeds but removal of the unencrypted snapshot fails, does the run stop checking and keeping the new backup, or continue and possibly keep it while reporting the run failed?
options: Stop the backup-producing step, leave only temporary files, then run rotation
Continue checking and rename a passing backup to its kept name, while the run remains failed
open_points.default_guess: Stop before checking or keeping the backup, then run rotation.

witness.initial: A due backup run has written and encrypted a consistent snapshot; the filesystem refuses deletion of the unencrypted snapshot.
events: module:backups attempts to remove the unencrypted snapshot.
The run proceeds according to one of the two readings of step 3.
outcomes: The new encrypted backup remains temporary and no backup for the date is kept.
The encrypted backup is checked and renamed, so a kept backup for the date exists although the run is reported failed.
witness.observer: The owner interface reading the newest kept backup and the owner monitoring the backup location
